output.evaluation_note: The Vietnamese term "giai cấp" primarily refers to "social class" or "economic stratum" (e.g., working class, bourgeoisie), which is a much narrower and more specific concept than the general English "rank" (position in a hierarchy, grade) or Japanese "階級" (kaikyū). It would be misleading for learners to equate "giai cấp" with the general sense of "rank" as in military rank, academic grade, or competition standing. More appropriate Vietnamese equivalents for the general sense of "rank" would be "cấp bậc", "thứ hạng", or "địa vị" depending on context.
